name: Staffordshire
description: Staffordshire is a centrally located county in the West Midlands known for its industrial heritage, pottery, ceramics and historic towns. Stafford, Stoke-on-Trent and Tamworth are major centres, while Cannock Chase and the Staffordshire Moorlands provide extensive countryside.

places.name: Lichfield
places.description: A cathedral city in Staffordshire notable for its three-spired medieval cathedral and as the birthplace of Samuel Johnson, compiler of one of the first English dictionaries.

places.name: Newcastle-under-Lyme
places.description: A market town in Staffordshire distinct from Newcastle upon Tyne, with a history tied to coal mining and pottery, and a well-preserved medieval street layout.

places.name: Staffordshire Moorlands
places.description: A district covering the southern Peak District fringes in Staffordshire, including the pottery town of Leek, known for its textile heritage.

places.name: Tamworth
places.description: A market town in Staffordshire, once the capital of the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, with a castle dating to the Norman period still standing above the town.

places.name: Cannock Chase
places.description: A district in Staffordshire named for its Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty — one of England's smallest AONBs — a stretch of ancient heathland and forest that was once a royal hunting ground.

places.name: East Staffordshire
places.description: A district around the brewing town of Burton upon Trent, long known as the historic centre of English beer production thanks to its mineral-rich water.

places.name: South Staffordshire
places.description: A rural district surrounding the Black Country conurbation, with villages and countryside offering a green contrast to the industrial towns nearby.

places.name: Stafford
places.description: The county town of Staffordshire, with a partly timber-framed medieval centre and strong historical ties to shoemaking.

places.name: Stoke-on-Trent
places.description: The heart of England's ceramics industry, historically known as 'The Potteries' for the six towns that merged to form the city, including famous names like Wedgwood and Spode.
